# Problem 1 

Using flowGate, go ahead and create your own series of gates for either our data or your own for any cell populations that might interest you. Once done, save the GatingSet, and then successfully reload it. Add another gate, but intentionally misdraw it. Then proceed to visualize, identify and correct it, before saving again.

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(flowWorkspace)
library(flowGate)
library(openCyto)

# Fetch data
folder <- file.path("data")
fcs_files <- list.files(folder, pattern = ".fcs", full.names = TRUE)

# Load data into GatingSet
cytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
gatingset <- GatingSet(cytoset)

# Apply biexponential transformation
Parameters <- colnames(gatingset)
FluorophoresOnly <- Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(Parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange = 4096, maxValue = 262144, pos = 4.5, neg = 2, widthBasis = -500)
BiexTransform <- transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)
flowWorkspace::transform(gatingset, BiexTransform)
ggcyto(gatingset[1], subset = "root", aes(x = "BUV805-A", y = "BV650-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

# Identify panel markers for gating strategy 
markernames(gatingset)
GatingTable <- tibble::tribble(
~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,      
  "singlets",   list("FSC-A", "FSC-H"),          "root",      
  "live",       list("FSC-A", "Zombie NIR-A"),   "singlets",  
  "Tcells",     list("CD3", "CD45"),              "live",     
"Mono",     list("FSC-A", "HLA-DR"),              "live",     
  "CD4+",       list("CD8", "CD4"),               "Tcells",   
  "CD8+",       list("CD8", "CD4"),               "Tcells",   
  "DN",         list("CD8", "CD4"),                "Tcells",  
"CD4Mem",       list("CD45RA", "CCR7"),               "CD4+",    
"CD8Mem",       list("CD45RA", "CCR7"),               "CD8+",  
  "Treg",       list("CD25", "CD127"),               "CD4+",   
  "Treg+",       list("CD25", "FoxP3"),               "Treg",  
  "MAIT",       list("CD161", "Va7.2"),               "Tcells",   
"CytoCD8",       list("CD8", "CD107a"),               "CD8+",   
)

# Apply gates
gs_apply_gating_strategy(gatingset, gating_strategy = GatingTable)
plot(gatingset)

# Save GatingSet
FolderandName <- file.path("/Users/Jessica.Williams/Downloads/Cytometry_in_R_Week08", "flowGateProblem1GS.gs")
save_gs(gatingset, FolderandName)

# Reload GatingSet
Reloadgs <- load_gs(FolderandName)
plot(Reloadgs)

# Add misdrawn gate
flowGate::gs_gate_interactive(gs=Reloadgs, filterId="CD161+", sample=1,
dims=list("CD161"), subset="CD8+")

# Visualise misdrawn gate
ggcyto::autoplot(Reloadgs[[1]]) + theme_bw()

# Rectify misdrawn gate
flowGate::gs_gate_interactive(gs=Reloadgs, filterId="CD161+", sample=1,
dims=list("CD161"), subset="CD8+", regate = TRUE)

ggcyto::autoplot(Reloadgs[[1]]) + theme_bw()

# Saving updated GatingSet
FolderandName <- file.path("/Users/Jessica.Williams/Downloads/Cytometry_in_R_Week08", "flowGateProblem1GS_CD161.gs")
save_gs(gatingset, FolderandName)
```

If you do plan to switch over to R for gating long-term, these skillsets will be essential, as you will need to be confident in your ability to adjust your gates as needed.

# Problem 2

Go ahead and create your own openCyto gate template, extending to whatever cell target population of interest. Visualize the differences, and ensure that the gates are correctly applied for everyone. Set gate_constaint arguments as needed until everything is just right.

```{r}
# Load openCyto gate template from .csv
Problem2GatingTemplate <- list.files(folder, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
GatingTemplate <- read.csv(Problem2GatingTemplate[2], check.names = FALSE)

# Load as data table for openCyto
GatesToApply <- data.table::fread(Problem2GatingTemplate[2])
FullTemplate <- gatingTemplate(GatesToApply)

# Prepare GatingSet
cytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
gatingset <- GatingSet(cytoset)
Parameters <- colnames(gatingset)
FluorophoresOnly <- Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(Parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange = 4096, maxValue = 262144, pos = 4.5, neg = 2, widthBasis = -500)
BiexTransform <- transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)
flowWorkspace::transform(gatingset, BiexTransform)

# Run gt_gating and visualise plots
gt_gating(FullTemplate, gatingset[6])

#PD1 gating showing 100% positive population using gate_mindensity - other method needed?
gt_list_methods()

#Used span_gate with min and max values in gating_args for more accruate gating
ggcyto::autoplot(gatingset[[6]]) + theme_bw()
```

If you do plan to switch over to R for gating long-term, these skillsets will be essential, as you will need to be confident in your ability to adjust your gates as needed.

**More gating method info can be found here: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/openCyto/inst/doc/HowToAutoGating.html#1D_gating_methods**

# Problem 3 

Re-run your openCyto template, but then add a few additional flowGate on to extend it further. Save the gating set, close out of positron, and successfully reload.

```{r}
# Re-run openCyto template
Problem2GatingTemplate <- list.files(folder, pattern = ".csv", full.names = TRUE)
GatesToApply <- data.table::fread(Problem2GatingTemplate[2])
FullTemplate <- gatingTemplate(GatesToApply)

cytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
gatingset <- GatingSet(cytoset)
Parameters <- colnames(gatingset)
FluorophoresOnly <- Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(Parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange = 4096, maxValue = 262144, pos = 4.5, neg = 2, widthBasis = -500)
BiexTransform <- transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)
flowWorkspace::transform(gatingset, BiexTransform)

gt_gating(FullTemplate, gatingset)
plot(gatingset)

# Add additional flow gates
AddingTable <- tibble::tribble(
~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,          
"Mono",     list("FSC-A", "HLA-DR"),              "live",      
  "Treg",       list("CD25", "CD127"),               "CD4",   
  "Treg+",       list("CD25", "FoxP3"),               "Treg",  
  "MAIT",       list("CD161", "Va7.2"),               "Tcells",     
)
gs_apply_gating_strategy(gatingset, gating_strategy = AddingTable)

# Plot final gating strategy
plot(gatingset)

# Save the gatingset
FolderandName <- file.path("/Users/Jessica.Williams/Downloads/Cytometry_in_R_Week08", "flowGateProblem3GS.gs")
save_gs(gatingset, FolderandName)

# Reload gatingset after Positron close down
library(ggplot2)
library(ggcyto)
library(flowWorkspace)
library(flowGate)
library(openCyto)

FolderandName <- file.path("/Users/Jessica.Williams/Downloads/Cytometry_in_R_Week08", "flowGateProblem3GS.gs")
Reloadgs <- load_gs(FolderandName)
plot(Reloadgs)
```
